topRisks.content: Insufficient product-related audits increase the likelihood that vulnerabilities and design flaws in the product go undetected.
Missing CCSS certification leaves crypto custody controls unvalidated, increasing the risk of undetected security gaps.
Lack of continuous on-chain monitoring lets abnormal fund flows go undetected, increasing the risk of delayed incident response.

reviews.text: Arbitrum is a leading layer-2 rollup on Ethereum, using optimistic tech for scaling. Launched in 2021, it has massive TVL in DeFi. In 2025, with Arbitrum One and Nova, it’s multi-chain ready. Governance is DAO-led. It’s reliable but has sequencer issues.

Arbitrum is a Layer 2 scaling solution for Ethereum that uses optimistic roll-up technology. Its goal is to reduce Ethereum's gas fees, increase transaction speed, and inherit security. The coin name is arb. The supply is 10 billion. 56.2 percent of it is in circulation. Founded by Offchain Labs, there are two main networks in the ARB ecosystem: Arbitrum Nova and Arbitrum One. Arbitrum one: The most widely used evm compatible optimistic roll up chain. Arbitrum Nova: A separate L2 with an Any Trust model optimized for social applications and low-cost projects.

Arbitrum is one of Ethereum’s largest Layer-2 networks, using optimistic rollup technology. It has two main networks: Arbitrum One (Used to run smart contracts, mostly for DeFi) and Arbitrum Nova (Used for applications that require a higher transaction throughput and don't require the full decentralization that rollups provide). Today, Arbitrum chains hold about $2.7 billion TVL in over 1000 protocols. Many dApps run on Arbitrum (GMX, Camelot DEX) and popular services (Robinhood Wallet, Magic Eden NFT marketplace) are integrated. As optimism, it is part of a group of superchains, with its Arbitrum Orbit, increasing its dominance all over the web3 space.
In the last months, due to the aggressive competition (Base, Optimism, BSC and other L1s), has lost much of its TVL, this is why it is always on spot, by launching grant programs to attract interest.

The platform comes as a layer 2 (L2 ), scaling solution for Ethereum. It seeks to improve the use of Ethereum network by improving  on some of its shortcomings, but relying on its security. The platform uses optimistic roll-up to achieve this, thereby presenting faster and cheaper transactions.

Arbitrum is an EVM compatible layer 2 scaling solution for Ethereum that uses optimistic rollup. Unlike the Optimism stacks that use single-round fault proofs, Arbitrum uses the Multi-Round, Interactive Fraud Proofs mechanism which is a more secure but potentially slower dispute although the same 7 days grace period. Moreover, Arbitrum allows developers to deploy code written in languages like Rust, C, and C++ alongside Solidity, all using the same execution environment.
Arbitrum was founded by highly experienced team members from Offchain Labs funded by top tier VCs like Polychain Capital, Pantera Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners. 
The protocol has secured partnerships with other web 3 protocols like Caldera, AltLayer and Conduit. Moreover, Arbitrum has employed excellent security measures including multiple up to date third party smart contract audits and an active bug bounty program with a maximum bounty of up to $2 Million.  Arbitrum has good potential  but Sequencer centralization, withdrawal delay and intense competition from other L 2 scaling solutions are the main challenges faced by the protocol.

Arbitrum has become my default Layer 2 for many things it’s battle tested and has huge trading volumes. I trust it because it’s also secured by Ethereum and it’s seen massive usage. The only wrinkle is that, like other Optimistic rollups, it uses a centralized sequencer initially, so there is a small trust issue. But overall, it feels like the closest thing to an official scaling layer today.

Arbitrum is a Layer2 scaling solution for Ethereum designed to improve transaction throughput and reduce fees while maintaining Ethereum’s security. By utilizing Optimistic Rollups, Arbitrum processes transactions off-chain before settling them on Ethereum, enabling faster and more cost-efficient transactions. Since its launch, Arbitrum has become one of the most popular Layer-2 solutions, attracting numerous decentralized applications (dApps) and users looking for a scalable Ethereum experience. With its focus on enhancing Ethereum’s capabilities, Arbitrum plays a crucial role in addressing the scalability challenges facing the Ethereum network.
